Axiom:
When a scope or module spec contains a Pivot Invalidation List, audit verifies every listed artifact has been addressed (scope `pivot` lists it in the scope spec; a breaking `refine-module` lists consumer modules in the module spec — same format, same check).
| Listed item | Check | Severity if stale | |---|---|---| | Module spec requiring `refine-module` | most recent Decision Log entry references the pivot `-DL-N` (or immutable legacy id) | `MAJOR` | | Task requiring reopen | Reopens counter incremented since pivot date, AND causally honest | `MAJOR` | | Rule to revisit | rule file mtime > pivot date | `MINOR` |
**"Causally honest" for the reopen row (`[REOPENS]`, B2-06) is now mechanical, not hand- counted** — take it as given, per `AX_MECHANICAL_VIA_SDD_CHECK`: `sdd-check --task` compares Meta `Reopens` against the number of persisted `@audit … triggered-reopen=Round-N` records in `## Audit Rounds`, and separately confirms every declared `triggered-reopen=Round-N` has a matching `### Round N` actually created in the Execution Log. A ticket whose ticket carries an audit round with `triggered-reopen=Round-2` while its Meta still reads `Reopens: 0` is exactly this: a reopen the audit process announced but the orchestrator never executed — the tool reports it as `SDD_REOPENS_MISMATCH` (Meta count wrong) and/or `SDD_REOPENS_PENDING` (Round 2 itself absent). Do not hand-re-derive this from the raw ticket text; the stale-pivot row above folds these tool findings in as its own evidence rather than re-counting `### Round` headers.
Epic-mode audit aggregates stale items into one summary finding. Greenfield/extension scopes without Pivot Invalidation List → check skipped silently.
